title: Exact quantum factoring
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's construction (2026) of a polynomial-time uniform family of quantum circuits over one fixed finite gate set (NOT, CNOT, Toffoli, the Hadamard gate and the phase gate S, with their inverses and singly controlled versions) that outputs the complete prime factorization of every integer N ≥ 2 with probability one. The first lesson fixes the model: uniform circuits, reversible evaluation, the unrolling of Turing machine computations, exact dyadic sampling, retained classical records and one step of amplitude amplification at probability one quarter. The second replaces the Fourier transform of order finding by a transform with a piecewise-linear interpolation of the exponential, realized exactly by controlled shifts of a phase register, and recovers fractions by continued fractions. The third corrects the probabilities of order sampling with a dyadic majorant whose sum is computed by exact power sums and with two classical modes, so that the order r of a unit is returned with probability exactly φ(r) 2^(−⌈log₂ r⌉−10). The fourth proves a deterministic polynomial-time primality test of Agrawal–Kayal–Saxena type. The fifth builds a factoring process whose completed runs also produce the factorizations of p − 1, recursively, from which the exact probability of a good output of each step is computed. The sixth makes the success probability exactly one quarter with filters computed after the data are verified, and proves the theorem.
prerequisites: finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces: unitary maps, orthogonal projections, tensor products
core course Abstract Algebra I (Judson): the integers (Theorem 2.2.7), Lagrange's theorem (Corollary 6.2.3), units modulo m (Theorems 6.3.1 and 6.3.3), orders in direct products (Corollary 9.2.6)

core course Abstract Algebra II (Judson): the Chinese remainder theorem (Theorem 16.5.3), roots of polynomials over a field (Corollary 17.2.4), extension fields (Theorem 21.1.5), finite fields (Lemma 22.1.3 and Corollary 22.1.11)
elementary real analysis: integration by parts, Riemann sums of Lipschitz functions
